correctness.rationale: The stationary crossing probabilities in both models are exactly U(x)=exp(-κx)/2. Direct spatial integration gives Gλ(z)=exp[-λLi₂((1-z)/2)], whose only unit-circle singularity is the logarithmic branch point z=-1. Expanding there yields -(λ/2)e^(-λπ²/6)(1+z)log(1+z), and logarithmic singularity transfer gives the alternating λe^(-λπ²/6)/(2n(n-1)) term with Oλ(log n/n³). An independent Pringsheim argument and Laplace periodicity establish that no positive law realizes this transform. The exact recurrence, low-order threshold and numerical values were executed in the attached standard-library script. Risk: asymptotic is fixed λ and the checker is finite only.

value.rationale: The original stationary quenched-current transform is widely used to describe a physical current and was said to be difficult to invert globally. The finding proves a universal all-parameter obstruction to interpreting that transform as any ordinary nonnegative law, derives a sharp alternating n^-2 tail, and identifies an explicit low-order failure region. It applies simultaneously to reset Brownian and reset run-and-tumble motion and clarifies exactly what true annealed or fixed-configuration probability laws retain. This is a structural interpretive boundary rather than an arbitrary negative entry.
